The current-screen oracle is `oracle-140.json` / `oracle-168.json`. From the checkout root, regenerate both with `python3 -m tools.fleet.tests.freeze_explorer_oracle` (or append `--check` to check without writing). It renders 19 synthetic states at each width through the current production renderer, including RESOURCES, detail pages and the unfolded session link. Language, time and beat are fixed; no live Fleet or collectors are started. `test_explorer_oracle.py` compares every cell and ordered hit without historical delta normalization, in both CI file execution and module discovery. Intentional screen changes should review and commit the regenerated snapshots.

The files below retain historical reference provenance. They are separate from the current-screen oracle and remain available to the parity and historical reference checks.

These fixtures use width-preserving synthetic text in place of freeform source content. cells-140.json and cells-168.json store each cell row as exact [glyph, colour_key, tint, count] runs. source.json points to view_model.json, which contains the same source values; long redacted strings use the fixture's transparent zlib/base85 encoding and test helpers decode them on load.

PEERS is exact like every other state: all cells and ordered hits at 140 and 168 columns, including the filtered f5 state. Its drawing data is general: `peer_edges.cards[tag].owners` carries the owner-stage rows the reference hand-writes per tag; the GPU and question lines, lane labels and the clear marker are derived from the session, question, link and seat records. The reference draws the repository-frame watch footer only for a repo named `hearting`; the scrubbed repo name differs, so the golden carries none and `peer_edges.watches` is empty here.

transitions.json is compact unindented JSON: cases store each viewer-main input chunk and a trace of state/frame references; shared frames intern identical frames, while the rows pool interns repeated cell rows stored as exact run-length records. Transition Every transition frame, PEERS included, compares all cells and ordered hits exactly. The manifest default is r14 DESIGN=4.

Repository-only test runs compare the committed goldens. Running freeze_explorer.py --check with the external approved reference directory re-verifies provenance using the input hashes in manifest.json. The reference renderer and PNGs are intentionally external; no private absolute path is stored here. default-once.json is captured separately from the archived base CLI.

The approved 2026-10-29 REPO-before-ID change updates the OVERVIEW/ROUTES tables and their repo/session page captures, including the compact route summary. Transition input chunks and navigation states stay unchanged; new table frames and rows are appended to the existing pools. PEERS captures and their transition frame payloads retain their exact prior contents. Cell and ordered-hit comparisons remain exact.

The approved 2026-10-31 display change puts the repo on the group rule once (OVERVIEW/ROUTES), grows HARNESS to the observed `harness (model·effort)` text, stacks steward targets under their steward with a grey dotted stalk, and shows frame legs at owner level. The external approved reference renderer was unavailable here, so the 2026-10-31 refresh against base commit `6d9d84a08` is renderer-generated rather than reference-verified, and the 2026-10-31 correction that followed it did not regenerate the goldens. The cell rule is honest but hybrid: in the owned states a cell moved only where the base renderer (`6d9d84a08`) and the current renderer differ, and every other cell keeps the committed base value. Page rows may therefore keep base fragments (for example a clipped model or age inside an owned page table) even though their state is owned; the oracle baseline at `6d9d84a08` already has 29 failing subcases (29 of 52 tests, 1 skipped), and those owned page rows are part of that known failing set, so they cannot serve as exact references. Non-owned states (QUESTIONS, HISTORY, COMPUTE/RESOURCES, MEMORY, MODELS, SYSTEM), sidebar tree rows and rules, the help/status rows and unrelated page rows remain byte-identical to `6d9d84a08`. Transition input chunks and navigation states stay unchanged; only owned frame cells and their ordered hits moved, while non-owned frames keep their prior payloads. The public fixture's `peer_edges` carries an empty `steward_columns` list for the shape contract, so the PEERS capture itself is unchanged.

The approved 2026-11-02 OVERVIEW change pulses the ROUTES rule's `N open` count on the shared working beat (`g_work`/`g_work_off`) while N > 0 and names the repo on every OVERVIEW ROUTES summary row instead of only the first of a run. transitions.json moved only those cells: the count cells on the ROUTES rule rows and the repo cells of repeated-repo summary rows (new pool rows appended). Transition input chunks, navigation states, hits and every other cell are unchanged.

The 2026-11-02 MEMORY change (Fleet usability design D4 #1) replaces the journal table and the BACKLOG block with one card per project: its newest decisions and open work from the stored headlines of the read-only DB summary, and its two newest journal rows. The fixture view model carries no DB summary, so its MEMORY frame shows each project's journal rows under `최근` and the status line names the unread DB. transitions.json moved only the two MEMORY frames (memory-row at 140 and 168; new pool rows appended); input chunks, navigation states and every other frame are unchanged. The cells-140/168.json MEMORY captures keep their prior contents: QuietReference already differs from the current renderer and the isolated runner does not run it.

The 2026-11-02 QUESTIONS board change names what each wait asks in plain English words (like the other Fleet screens) in the last column (now headed QUESTION; a title-carrying reference record still shows its title there), lists the who/when/route lines (`route:`, `since:`, `owner:`) under an unfolded wait instead of `source:`/`kind:`, widens KIND so `blocked owner` fits, and lists older waits until the person folds them. transitions.json moved only the QUESTIONS frames of the questions-toggle (140, 168) and questions-answer-fold (140) cases: new frames and rows are appended to the pools and those steps point at them (`refreeze_transitions.py` does exactly this for any intended screen change; transitions.json is one line, so after a merge conflict take either side and run it again). Input chunks, navigation states and every other frame are unchanged. The cell goldens (cells-140/168.json) are not run by the isolated runner and are left as they were.

The `attempts` record carries the route it belongs to (`route`: f5). The reference draws one owner's raw output, on that route's page; the live builder names the route of the owner output the selection reader returned, so a route page never shows another route's lines.

A route record may carry `detail_title`, `detail_trailer` and `detail_after`: the words on the top band of an opened route and the note beside its stage band, which the reference words apart from the row's own title and age for some routes. A source without them gets the derived words.

parity_matrix.py compares the same view model with the approved reference for every state the reference's own click targets reach, at 80, 100, 140 and 168 columns; where the reference overlaps or overflows itself the rows are excluded and Fleet must draw clean there.
